title: Number of Singaporeans Provided Childcare, Preschool and After-school Care Subsidies
what_it_is: Number of Singaporeans Provided Childcare, Preschool and After-school Care Subsidies

sections.label: Childcare subsidy questions for families
sections.summary: An MP asks about numbers of Singaporeans receiving childcare, preschool and after-school care subsidies, extending subsidies to non-working mothers, and reviewing ECDA subsidies and means testing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what is the current number of Singaporeans who have been provided with childcare/preschool and after-school care subsidies respectively, broken down by (i) income group (ii) amount of subsidy and (iii) the after-subsidy fee they are paying; (b) whether the Ministry will extend the subsidies to non-working mothers who look after other elder children in the family; and (c) whether the Ministry will review the subsidies given by ECDA centres in providing childcare/preschool and after-school care and also consider eliminating means testing so that all parents pay a uniform fee.

sections.label: Median subsidy and nett fee
sections.summary: For this group, the median total subsidy is $560 with a median nett fee of $210, and the median total subsidy is $767 with a median nett fee of $3.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: For this group, the median total subsidy is $560 and the median nett fee after subsidy is $210.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: For this group, the median total subsidy is $767 and the median nett fee is $3.

sections.label: Childcare subsidy income ceiling raised
sections.summary: In January 2020 the household income ceiling for Childcare Additional Subsidy and KiFAS was raised to $12,000 per month from $7,500 and $6,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In January 2020, we raised the household income ceiling for the Childcare Additional Subsidy and KiFAS to $12,000 per month, up from $7,500 and $6,000 respectively, to support more families with pre-school expenses.

sections.label: Incentivising families with more children
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government will also consider incentivising families who have more children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My question is: will the Government also consider incentivising families who have more children?

sections.label: Reason for encouraging more babies
sections.summary: Encouraging more babies is one reason why it was done, but not the reason to do it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Encouraging more babies is one reason why we did it, but not the reason to do it.

sections.label: Higher subsidies for students above seven
sections.summary: Students above seven years old who need care because of their family circumstances have access to higher subsidies given the special circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: For students above seven years old who need care because of the circumstances in their families, they have access to higher subsidies given the special circumstances the families may need.
